_README: Fourth held-out set, written 2026-10-03 BEFORE any dev result for the changes it certifies existed: the guardrail review list (no bare refusal), IPC definition -> punishing section, and the dual candidate list (fused + statute text). Held-out 3 was spent finding the problems those changes address.

A mix: offences outside the corpus's four core families (defamation, mischief by fire, wrongful restraint, outraging modesty, kidnapping, forgery, confinement, intimidation) and core ones (cheating, hurt, house-breaking theft, dowry cruelty), both eras. Cases 13 and 14 are purely civil controls, ungated.
HELD OUT. Committed before any run. Score once with scripts/eval_broad.py and re-score with scripts/score_runs.py. Never tune on it.

Synthetic facts. Section ids checked against the ingested statutes by scripts/check_fixture_ids.py; `relevant` is Claude's legal call, NOT reviewed by a lawyer. `arguable` sections are not counted against the pipeline.

cases.query: At a village meeting attended by about forty people, the accused stood up and said that the complainant, the village schoolteacher, had stolen the money collected for the school's new roof. No money was missing, and the accused knew the collection had been deposited in the bank.

cases.offence_type: assault on a woman to outrage modesty
cases.query: In a crowded market the accused came up behind the complainant, a young woman, grabbed her by the waist and pulled her scarf off while laughing with his friends, and ran off when she screamed.
After a quarrel over irrigation water, the accused went to the complainant's field at night and set fire to his stacked wheat harvest, destroying produce worth about eighty thousand rupees.

The complainant uses a village path to reach his own field. The accused parked his tractor across the path and stood in front of it, telling the complainant he would not be allowed to pass that way to his field.

Within a year of the marriage, the husband and his mother repeatedly beat the complainant and told her she would not be allowed to stay in the house unless her father paid two lakh rupees more and gave them a car.

The accused advertised a new mobile phone on a social media page, took twenty-two thousand rupees from the complainant by bank transfer, never sent the phone, and then blocked the complainant's number and deleted the page.
The complainant had refused to sell his shop to the accused. The accused phoned him twice and said that if he did not sign the sale papers by Sunday he would be killed and his sons would be next.
At about two in the morning the accused removed the iron grill of a window, climbed into the complainant's house while the family slept, and took gold jewellery and cash from a cupboard.

The accused prepared a sale deed for the complainant's plot, signed the complainant's name on it himself, and got it registered in his own favour at the sub-registrar's office, then tried to sell the plot to a third person.

The accused, a stranger, waited outside a primary school, told a nine-year-old girl that her mother had sent him to fetch her, and took her away on his motorcycle without her parents' knowledge. She was found two days later in another town.
Two men to whom the complainant owed money took him to a godown, locked him inside overnight and released him the next morning only after he signed a promissory note.
During an argument over a parking space, the accused slapped the complainant twice and punched him in the face, giving him a bruised cheek.
Because of a cash shortage the small company paid its staff their March salary six weeks late. All the money has now been paid, and one employee wants interest for the delay.

Branches of the neighbour's tree hang over the complainant's wall and drop leaves into his courtyard. He has asked the neighbour to trim them, the neighbour says the tree is on his land and he will not.
